I need to check the tabs component source to verify whether inactive TabsContent stays mounted, since that determines the real re-render cost across S3, backup, and about tabs. I'm also noting that the effect resetting state on `[isOpen]` means closing the modal via Esc or overlay click silently discards unsaved edits, since the save button only lives in the models tab header.

I also spot a confirmed bug where the "设置已保存" success message lingers after a save even once the user makes new unsaved edits, since nothing clears it except reopening the modal. And `persistRegistry` seems to require at least one image and one text model configured, which would block users who only want image generation.

I also notice image models fall back to aioss.cc when Base URL is cleared and saved, defaulting silently. Tracing the code path confirms it: normalizeImageModelConfig fills in the aioss.cc baseUrl during save, so the relay's key silently ends up bound to the wrong host after reload, and this same fallback also applies to text models regardless of their intended endpoint.

This is disclosed in the UI itself ("文本模型固定调用 aioss.cc"), so it's a known limitation rather than a hidden bug, though it's worth flagging that first-party provider keys get forwarded to a third-party relay. I want to verify the claim that the settings UI still shows an editable Base URL field for text models — checking SettingsModal.tsx around lines 777-832 shows no such field exists in the current source, so I need to check where createTextModel comes into play.

Actually, I found another leak vector: `handleUpdateImageModel` with a builtin preset overwrites name, modelId, baseUrl, and limits outright. If a user had typed a custom relay Base URL and key, then selects a preset, their Base URL resets to the default host while keeping their API key — meaning their relay key could get sent to the wrong host unnoticed. The fix should only fill empty/default fields, never clobber a user-customized baseUrl. The same pattern likely applies to text models when switching protocol and applying the template.

Also noting the max resolution options are capped by the preset's maxOutputSize rather than the actual model, so a custom model on a low-res preset can't select higher resolutions even if supported — possibly intentional, but worth flagging alongside the unbounded maxRefImages field.

I'm also realizing capabilities are driven by the preset ID while request routing is driven by protocol, so users could create mismatched combos, like an openai-style preset paired with a google protocol, potentially producing invalid parameter combinations — a lower-priority but real inconsistency worth noting before I move on to checking how the model registry is read.

For the "check models" flow, I'm confirming it reads the saved registry, not the draft, so unsaved new models get filtered out and the UI renders an empty grid with no explanatory message, while edited key/baseURL fields get checked against stale saved values causing false positives or negatives. This is a real SSRF issue — an attacker could point baseUrl at internal hosts like the AWS metadata endpoint, and the upstream JSON response gets returned to the caller, giving readback. Desktop mode is safer since it binds to localhost with a session token, but the web-mode exposure is a legitimate high-severity finding worth flagging.

Evidence: [ccode-task-client.ts:252](frontend/src/lib/ccode-task-client.ts:252) builds the key into the URL and uses plain `fetch`; [server.js:2201](backend/server.js:2201) sends `null`; [server.js:128](backend/server.js:128) sets the timeout. Fix: send a POST, add a 20 s timeout, write plain-language errors, and add a test-generate action.

7. Closing the dialog silently throws away edits (Medium-high, verified). Nothing tracks unsaved changes, so every close goes through and the next open reloads saved data. Deletes aren't confirmed, "设置已保存" stays on screen after new edits, and preferences save instantly while models need the button. Evidence: [SettingsModal.tsx:550](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:550) closes unconditionally; [SettingsModal.tsx:189](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:189) reloads on open; [SettingsModal.tsx:362](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:362) never clears the success message. Fix: track unsaved changes, confirm on close, add a sticky save bar and confirm deletes.

8. Users with only image models can't save (Medium, verified). Save requires a complete image model and a complete text model, and `hasAnyApiKey` checks both with `&&`. Evidence: [SettingsModal.tsx:335](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:335); [settings-storage.ts:31](frontend/src/lib/settings-storage.ts:31). Fix: require one complete model and gate text features separately.

9. Save failures and corrupt data aren't handled (Medium, verified by reading). `persistRegistry` has no try/catch, but desktop throws when OS encryption is unavailable. `loadRegistry` calls `JSON.parse` without a guard, so one corrupt value breaks every caller. Evidence: [secret-store.js:18](desktop/storage/secret-store.js:18) throws; [SettingsModal.tsx:358](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:358) calls `saveRegistry` unguarded; [nova-models.ts:375](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:375). Fix: catch the error and show it, and fall back to an empty registry with a notice.

10. Default models change silently and don't change back (Medium, verified). An invalid default jumps to the first complete model, and the image-to-image fallback ignores `maxRefImages`. This check reruns on every keystroke, so briefly clearing the default model's key switches the default to another model for good. Evidence: [nova-models.ts:347](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:347); [SettingsModal.tsx:239](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:239). Fix: recheck defaults only on save, require `maxRefImages > 0` for image-to-image, and tell the user when a default changes.

11. Base URL validation gaps (Medium, verified). There's no URL or scheme check. Only a trailing `/v1` is stripped (Google: `/v1beta`) before fixed paths are added. So pasted full endpoints, Google URLs ending in `/v1`, and `/api/v3` relays all break. Evidence: [model-endpoints.ts:17](frontend/src/lib/model-endpoints.ts:17); [server.js:1189](backend/server.js:1189) appends `/v1/images/...`. Fix: parse with `new URL`, require http(s), strip known suffixes and show a preview of the final URL.

12. On desktop, reading the registry blocks the UI (Medium, verified by reading). Each `loadRegistry()` is a synchronous IPC call that decrypts every key, and helpers don't cache it. One `GenerationParamsBar` render can make up to 12 of these calls with GPT Image 2 at a fixed size. The ratio check also looks up the hard-coded ID `'gpt-image-2'`, which never matches the IDs the app generates. Evidence: [preload.js:15](desktop/preload.js:15) `sendSync`; [storage-service.js:86](desktop/storage/storage-service.js:86); [GenerationParamsBar.tsx:60](frontend/src/components/GenerationParamsBar.tsx:60); [model-capabilities.ts:194](frontend/src/lib/model-capabilities.ts:194). Fix: cache the registry, refresh it on `nova-model-registry-updated`, and read keys only when sending a request.

13. Missing relay features (Medium, verified). There's no per-model streaming toggle: text clients always send `stream: true`, and image streaming is one global env setting. There are also no custom headers, per-model timeout, path override, test-generate button, or model export/import/duplicate that leaves keys out. Evidence: [reverse-prompt-client.ts:76](frontend/src/lib/reverse-prompt-client.ts:76); [server.js:129](backend/server.js:129) `NOVA_IMAGE_STREAM`; [server.js:2089](backend/server.js:2089) fixed auth headers. Fix: add optional per-model `stream`, `headers`, `timeoutMs` and `pathOverride`.

14. Settings modal re-renders a lot per keystroke (Low, verified by reading). It's one component of 1,100+ lines with 27 `useState` calls. Every keystroke reruns the defaults check, which does two `JSON.stringify` calls, and rebuilds every dropdown's options. The tabs library unmounts inactive panels, which keeps the cost down. Evidence: [SettingsModal.tsx:243](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:243); [SettingsModal.tsx:540](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:540).
